data.one_liner: Makes --dart-define and --dart-define-from-file variables available to native Android and iOS platforms.
data.what_it_does: Provides compile-time environment variables set via Flutter build flags directly to native platform files like Android's build.gradle, manifests, and Kotlin code, as well as iOS plist and Swift files.
use_when: You need access to dart-define environment variables inside native Android (Gradle/Kotlin/Manifest) or iOS (plist/Swift) code.
You want to configure native app names, keys, or endpoints using a .env file passed via --dart-define-from-file.
avoid_when: You only need environment variables within Dart code and do not require them on the native side.
You cannot make the required native configuration changes in build.gradle, Podfile, or Info.plist.
strengths: Bridges Dart compile-time variables with native Android and iOS configurations.
weaknesses: Requires manual configuration and modifications to native project files (build.gradle, Podfile, AndroidManifest.xml, Info.plist).
iOS xcconfig has limitations with certain characters like '//'.
data.setup_notes: Requires editing android/app/build.gradle, AndroidManifest.xml, MainActivity.kt, ios/Podfile, and info.plist.
